name: Solomon Hykes
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded dotCloud (the company that later became Docker, Inc.) in 2008 in Paris/Montrouge with Sebastien Pahl, building a multi-language PaaS that would pivot into the Docker container project.
early_history_summary: Born in New York City to an American father and French-Canadian mother, Hykes moved to France at age four and coded from childhood, including running servers at an internet cafe as a teenager in exchange for free access. He studied at Epitech in Paris (entered 2001), worked briefly in security and media tech, then co-founded dotCloud in 2008 at age 25 before gaining Y Combinator acceptance in 2010.
family_context_summary: Born in NYC to an American father and French-Canadian mother; raised in France from age four. Family financial status not detailed beyond later working from his mother's house near Paris during early startup years.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech-domain experts; father was American and Hykes spoke English with him. No clear parental tech apprenticeship documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Epitech, early coding, cofounder Pahl, PaaS/container wave, YC later
evidence_summary: Hykes built deep systems-programming practice from childhood through Epitech project work and early employment. Co-founding dotCloud at 25 created the platform that later open-sourced Docker in 2013, riding the cloud/container wave. Y Combinator (2010) and Silicon Valley relocation accelerated distribution after the age-26 window. Family domain and capital advantages are weakly documented; primary edge was technical depth plus cofounder execution.
starting_point: Born in New York City in 1983 to an American father and French-Canadian mother; raised in France from age four with early self-taught programming.
current_position: Founder of Dagger (programmable CI/CD engine); former founder/CTO of Docker, Inc.; lives in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.event: Entered Epitech in Paris and deepened software-engineering practice through project-based training.
Co-founded dotCloud with Sebastien Pahl as a multi-language PaaS company in the Paris area.
Accepted into Y Combinator with dotCloud; raised angel capital including from Jerry Yang and Ron Conway.
Open-sourced Docker container technology and renamed the company Docker, Inc., sparking industry-wide adoption.
Docker reached unicorn valuation after large venture rounds and partnerships with Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and IBM.
Stepped down as Docker CTO while remaining on the board of the then multi-billion-valued company.
Launched public beta of Dagger, a new DevOps/CI platform built around containers.

name: Biz Stone
milestone_by_age_26: Helped form and served as creative director of Xanga (1999–2001), an early blogging/social journaling platform, at age 25–27—his first material product leadership role in consumer internet media.
early_history_summary: Born Christopher Isaac Stone in Boston on March 10, 1974; raised in Wellesley, Massachusetts largely by his mother on constrained means after parents divorced. Attended Northeastern and UMass Boston without graduating; worked at Little, Brown as a designer, then became Xanga creative director in 1999, later joined Google's Blogger team, and co-founded Twitter in 2006.
family_context_summary: Father Christopher Stone was a Boston auto mechanic who was largely absent after divorce; mother Marjory Pugh raised Biz and three sisters in Wellesley, at times depending on welfare. Modest economic circumstances.
parent_family_domain_summary: No parental tech or media domain expertise documented; father was a mechanic, mother not in software/media entrepreneurship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Xanga early blog wave, design taste, later Google/Blogger network, Twitter cofounders
evidence_summary: Stone's age-25 Xanga creative-director role on a pioneering blog community established him in consumer web product design before Google Blogger and Twitter. Family background shows economic constraint rather than inherited capital or domain. Later Twitter co-founding (2006, age 32) made him globally famous; early edge was product/design taste plus immersion in early blogging platforms.
starting_point: Born 1974 in Boston; raised in Wellesley, Massachusetts primarily by mother Marjory Pugh under financial strain after parents' divorce; father was an auto mechanic.
current_position: Twitter/X co-founder; angel investor and advisor; joined Mastodon US nonprofit board (2024); lives in Marin County, California with wife Livia.

trajectory.event: Joined friends to form Xanga and served as creative director of the early blogging community through 2001.
Joined Google's Blogger team in a senior product/design leadership role after a brief stint at Wellesley College.
Co-founded Twitter with Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, and Evan Williams; held creative director role.
Named among Time 100 Most Influential People as Twitter's public profile exploded.
Left Twitter to pursue new ventures and later co-founded Jelly (acquired by Pinterest in 2017).
Returned to Twitter in a strategic capacity; remained until around 2021.
Joined the board of Mastodon's U.S. nonprofit entity.

name: Near (programmer)
milestone_by_age_26: Launched the bsnes project on October 14, 2004 (age 21), building the first Super Nintendo emulator to pursue and later achieve 100% library compatibility through cycle-accurate hardware emulation; earlier completed Dragon Quest V fan translation in November 2001 (age 18).
early_history_summary: David Kirk Ginder (pseudonyms Near / byuu), born February 22, 1983, entered fan translation as a teenager, self-taught assembly and tooling from age ~14–16, completed Dragon Quest V localization in 2001, and started bsnes in 2004 after hardware-accuracy failures on Der Langrisser. Later created higan, invented the MSU-1 mapper, and led major SNES preservation work before dying by suicide in Tokyo in 2021 after sustained online harassment.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond American origin and later life in Japan.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen ROM hacking, online emulation community, obsessive accuracy practice, peer collaborators
evidence_summary: Near accumulated exceptional SNES assembly and emulation practice from the mid-teens through completed fan translations by age 18 and the 2004 launch of bsnes at 21. Edge came from self-directed online community immersion and extreme concentration rather than elite institutions or family capital. bsnes/higan set the accuracy standard for SNES emulation and enabled preservation and even Stephen Hawking speech-synthesizer work derived from related cores.
starting_point: Born February 22, 1983, in the United States; early life and family class background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died by suicide on June 27, 2021, in Arakawa, Tokyo, at age 38; final work included Bahamut Lagoon localization and SNES preservation.

trajectory.event: Completed Dragon Quest V fan translation after intensive assembly reprogramming work.
Launched the bsnes project on October 14, pursuing hardware-accurate Super Nintendo emulation.
bsnes accuracy work and community recognition peaked as the project approached full SNES library compatibility.
Sold a complete North American SNES collection to fund broader multi-region game preservation scanning.
Stepped back from public emulation scene after escalating harassment and privacy intrusions.
Released Bahamut Lagoon fan translation; died by suicide in Tokyo on June 27 after prolonged online abuse.
